summary: Jefferson County, WA ground cab on Mount Jupiter (Olympic NF), built 1933-34, burned or removed 1967-68; one small remnant reportedly remains in the summit rocks.

facts.design: R-6 standard plan, 14x14 ft wood-frame ground house (register lists it as a gable-roof L-4 ground cab)
facts.status_note: Cab burned or removed 1967-68; SummitPost says one small remnant is embedded in the summit rocks

staffing.status: staffed in 1956 and 1958 per a former colleague's account; 1956 newspaper report says the station was still snowed in on July 7

access.note: Hiking trail of about 7 miles to the summit; access road is rough and a wildlife gate on it is closed Oct 1 to May 1

visit.trail_note: About 7.2 miles on the Jupiter Ridge trail (Willhite); long road walk through a logging operation to the trailhead (WTA); check with the Quilcene Ranger District about the gate (SummitPost)

events.note: Built 1933 per the register and firelookout.com; Willhite says 1933 or 1934; Forest Lookouts says 1934
Port Angeles Evening News, July 7, 1956: station still snowed in while other Quilcene district stations were manned; a former colleague's account says a friend was hired for the summer
Former colleague's account says the lookout was staffed again in summer 1958
Register: intentionally burned circa 1967; photo caption says intentionally burned in 1967 or 68
Forest Lookouts: 1968, the lookout was removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1933 per the register and firelookout.com; 1933 or 1934 per Willhite; 1934 per Forest Lookouts. The record keeps 1933 and the story notes the others.
The register calls it a gable-roof L-4 ground cab; Forest Lookouts quotes a standard R-6 plan, 14x14 feet. Both descriptions are sourced; the R-6 record value is kept.
Year of loss is 1967 (register, firelookout.com), 1967 or 68 (Willhite), and 1968 (Forest Lookouts). Only the register describes a deliberate burn.

notes_for_editor: Built year (1933 vs 1934) and fate year (1967 vs 1968) disagree across sources; design conflict (L-4 vs R-6) is shown in resolved_conflicts. The remnant claim comes from SummitPost, a trip-report page, not a survey. Brief height_m 4.3 is not supported by any page read here, so it is omitted. The FFLOS registration date (Feb 19, 2011) was not visible in the text read, so no fflos_registered event. Read budget for this tower was exceeded (about 9 page reads) to check the remnant and gate claims. Fact-check 2026-10-09: removed the sentence saying other sources show no remains (no evidence quote backs it); the remnant claim stays attributed to SummitPost.
